items.title: Slim Third-Ballot Win Makes Navdeep Bains the New Ontario Liberal Leader
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, former Mississauga and Brampton MP Navdeep Bains has won the Ontario Liberal Party leadership, prevailing by a narrow margin in a third round of voting on Nov. 21. The party says more than 20,500 members cast ballots, a 15 per cent increase in turnout from the previous leadership race. Bains spent years moving between federal politics, teaching and the private sector before entering the provincial race. In a statement following the result, Bains said he was honoured by the trust Ontario Liberals placed in him and declared the party ready for what he called Ontario's moment.

items.title: Mississauga's Election Sign Ban Faces Charter Challenge As Rights Group Intervenes
items.summary: According to the Canadian Constitution Foundation, the group has been granted leave to intervene in a court challenge against the City of Mississauga's total ban on election signs on public property. The case was brought by longtime political candidate Greg Vezina, whose campaign signs were removed from public property under the city's by-law in 2019. Vezina argues the by-law is a content-based restriction, since the city allows other signs, such as those advertising housing developments and farmers' markets, while banning only election signs. His application will proceed to a hearing at the Superior Court of Justice over whether the ban violates free expression under the Charter. CCF interim litigation director Josh Dehaas said sign bans disadvantage lesser known candidates, since signs are one of the few affordable ways to reach voters against established politicians.

items.title: Toronto Police Say Mississauga Man Used Fake Badge to Pose as Officer at Etobicoke Park
items.summary: According to Toronto Police, a Mississauga man employed as a correctional officer at the Toronto South Detention Centre is accused of posing as a police officer during an encounter at Colonel Sam Smith Park in Etobicoke this past Sunday. Police say the man approached occupants of a vehicle in the parking lot, identified himself as an Ontario Provincial Police officer and displayed a metal badge. He then demanded identification from the occupants and directed them to exit the vehicle, according to police. Responding officers located a suspect near the scene shortly afterward, police said in a news release. Joshia Jiju Koshy, 21, of Mississauga, was arrested and charged, and is scheduled to appear at the Ontario Court of Justice in Toronto on Feb. 16, 2027.

items.title: Mississauga Budget Committee Set to Weigh MiWay Fare Hike This Week
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga's budget committee will consider a proposal this week to raise MiWay transit fares starting Jan. 1, 2027. Senior city staff are recommending the increase to help offset rising costs tied to inflation, labour, maintenance and service delivery, according to a report set for Wednesday's meeting. The report notes MiWay still faces a revenue shortfall despite previous fare adjustments. Sam Rogers, the city's commissioner of transportation and works, said in the report that the proposed changes reflect a balanced approach to current revenue and ridership realities. City councillors are expected to debate the recommendation before any fare changes take effect.

items.title: Mississauga Arrest Closes In On Suspects Behind Welland Jewelry Store Break-In Attempt
items.summary: According to Niagara Regional Police, a Brampton man wanted in an attempted break-in at a jewelry store near Niagara Falls was arrested in Mississauga by Peel Regional Police on Monday. Police say he is now in custody awaiting a court appearance, and a second suspect is held by another police service pending transfer to Niagara police. Both men are suspects in an Oct. 26 attempted break-in at a jewelry store near Thorold Road and Prince Charles Drive in Welland, southwest of Niagara Falls. Police say a white Volkswagen Touareg SUV was used to ram the front of the business. The suspects could not get inside and fled in a black Audi Q7 at high speed before police arrived, Niagara police said in a news release. Detectives said two masked men were involved, and the building sustained significant damage, prompting a structural engineer to assess it.

items.title: City of Mississauga Says 311 Resolved Most Resident Calls Without Follow-Up Last Year
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, 311 serves as the city's customer service hub for non-emergency information and service requests, from pothole reports to questions about property standards. The city says residents can reach the service by phone, online, in person or through social media, with phone support available in more than 240 languages and dialects. A teletypewriter line at 905-896-5151 is also available for people with hearing or speech-related disabilities, the city says. Contacting 311 directly ensures a request enters the city's official system and can be tracked for follow-up, improving accountability, according to the city. The city reports that 73 per cent of calls in 2025 were resolved at the first point of contact, with no further action required.

items.title: City Warns Feeding Coyotes and Other Wildlife Carries a $365 Fine in Mississauga
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, feeding wildlife such as coyotes, foxes, squirrels and birds is illegal and carries a $365 fine for a first offence, with higher penalties for repeat violations. The city says the animals can find food on their own and do not need help from residents, even when the gesture seems kind. Officials warn that regularly fed wild animals can lose their natural fear of people, linger in busy areas or approach people looking for food. The city points to coyotes specifically, saying one that learns to associate people with food may begin approaching people rather than keeping its distance. The simplest way to help wildlife, according to the city, is to leave it alone entirely.

items.title: Second Officer Tells Francique Inquest Surveillance, Not a Planned Arrest, Was Underway That Night
items.summary: According to testimony at the coroner's inquest into the death of Jamal Francique, Det. Mani Sharifi said police had no plan to arrest Francique on the night he was fatally shot in 2020. Sharifi told the inquest officers moved in only after they observed Francique breaching his bail conditions by leaving his home. The real plan, Sharifi said, was to continue surveillance that had already been underway for roughly three or four days until an opportunity arose. A juror asked why Francique was not arrested earlier in the week, once officers first saw him breach his bail, and Sharifi said his unit was instead focused on investigating whether Francique possessed a firearm or was involved in drug activity. Francique was shot by an officer outside a Mississauga townhouse complex on the evening of Jan. 7, 2020, according to the inquest.

items.title: Dixie Road Shut Down in Both Directions After Crash Involving a Police Cruiser
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Paramedic Services, one person was taken to hospital with minor, non-life threatening injuries after a two-vehicle collision involving a police cruiser in Mississauga on Monday night. Paramedics say the crash happened on Dixie Road north of Rathburn Road. The other driver involved remained at the scene, paramedics said. Dixie Road is currently closed in both directions between Rathburn Road and Burnhamthorpe Road while crews respond, according to police. Police are asking motorists to seek alternate routes while the road remains closed.

items.title: Rooftop Solar and Two EVs Help Mississauga Couple Cut Energy Bills Well Below National Average
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, Mississauga residents Harminder Dhillon and Jyoti Grewal say they spent roughly $1,100 in 2025 to power their home and run two electric vehicles. The couple installed rooftop solar panels, disconnected natural gas service, switched to heat pumps and an induction stove, and replaced gas powered cars with electric ones, bringing their reported costs to about $92 a month. Canadian households spent an average of $4,943 on energy in 2023, according to Natural Resources Canada's Energy Fact Book. The outlet notes the figures come from different years and are not a direct comparison, since energy costs vary with home size and local rates. Dhillon, an engineer turned criminal lawyer, says the switch began as a response to climate change rather than an effort to save money, describing it to CityNews as a climate decision, not a financial one.
